question: Proven techniques for building a cute stylized 3D character in three.js from code (no imported model) and making it feel alive, cheaply enough for a phone: stylized materials and cheap shadows, procedural construction and outlines, alive-animation techniques and libraries, image-to-voxel InstancedMesh.

claims.claim: MeshMatcapMaterial gets its whole look (color plus shading) from one matcap texture, so a glossy vinyl-toy look can be baked into a single image.
claims.quote: This material is defined by a MatCap (or Lit Sphere) texture, which encodes the material color and shading.

claims.claim: MeshMatcapMaterial ignores scene lights (no per-light shading cost), because lighting is baked in the matcap image.
claims.quote: MeshMatcapMaterial does not respond to lights since the matcap image file encodes baked lighting.

claims.claim: A matcap mesh can cast a shadow but never receives one or self-shadows, so grounding a matcap character needs a separate shadow receiver (ground plane or fake blob).
claims.quote: It will cast a shadow onto an object that receives shadows (and shadow clipping works), but it will not self-shadow or receive shadows.

claims.claim: MeshToonMaterial banding is controlled by gradientMap, and the gradient texture must use NearestFilter for both minFilter and magFilter (otherwise the steps blur).
claims.quote: Gradient map for toon shading. It's required to set Texture#minFilter and Texture#magFilter to NearestFilter when using this type of texture.

claims.claim: The official three.js contact-shadow example (webgl_shadow_contact) renders scene depth from below with an upward-looking orthographic camera into a 512 x 512 px render target, using a patched MeshDepthMaterial that outputs black with depth-based alpha. Quote is a code line relayed by the fetch summarizer, not read raw; recheck against the file before relying on exact text.
claims.quote: shadowCamera.rotation.x = Math.PI / 2; // get the camera to look up

claims.claim: The same contact-shadow example softens the depth texture with a two-pass (horizontal then vertical) blur ping-ponged between two 512 x 512 px render targets, run twice per frame (once at blur, once at blur * 0.4; default blur 3.5). So its per-frame cost is one extra scene render plus four full-screen-quad blur passes at 512 px. Quote is a code comment relayed by the fetch summarizer.

CapsuleGeometry exists in core for rounded limbs/bodies; signature CapsuleGeometry(radius=1, height=1, capSegments=4, radialSegments=8, heightSegments=1), where height is the middle section only (total length = height + 2*radius). Default 8 radial segments is visibly faceted, so raise it for a smooth toy look.
claims.quote: Number of segmented faces around the circumference of the capsule. Must be an integer >= 3.

claims.claim: LatheGeometry revolves a 2D profile around the Y axis (signature LatheGeometry(points, segments=12, phiStart=0, phiLength=Math.PI*2)), suitable for a custom rounded body/head silhouette that a sphere or capsule cannot give.
claims.quote: Creates meshes with axial symmetry like vases. The lathe rotates around the Y axis.

claims.claim: LatheGeometry profile points must have x greater than zero, which constrains how the profile is closed at the poles.
claims.quote: An array of points in 2D space. The x-coordinate of each point must be greater than zero.

claims.claim: OutlinePass is a post-processing pass (needs EffectComposer and extra render targets) for selected objects; it can run at reduced resolution, downSampleRatio default 2.
claims.quote: The downsample ratio. The effect can be rendered in a much lower resolution than the beauty pass.

claims.claim: three.js ships OutlineEffect, an outline addon aimed at toon shading (defaultThickness 0.003, defaultColor [0,0,0]); it is WebGLRenderer-only and replaces the normal render call.
claims.quote: Note that this class can only be used with WebGLRenderer. When using WebGPURenderer, use ToonOutlinePassNode.

claims.claim: A rim/fresnel term can be added to a built-in material by string-replacing a shader chunk in onBeforeCompile-style code and passing a view direction and a view-space normal as varyings (forum code by prisoner849; the fragment-side rim math itself was only in linked fiddles, not on the page).

maath (pmndrs) main-branch API.md now documents a spring module for secondary motion: spring.update(state, target, smoothTime, dampingRatio, delta) mutates a {value, velocity} state in place; spring.damp(state, target, smoothTime, delta) is the critically damped case; spring.dampAngle takes the shortest angular path; spring2/spring3/spring4 are the vector versions. A dampingRatio below 1 gives overshoot (jiggle).
claims.quote: Springs `state.value` toward `target`, mutating `state` in place. Returns it.

claims.claim: GSAP's default ease is power1.out; its core ease list on the same page includes back, bounce and elastic, the overshoot eases used for squash-and-stretch and follow-through.
claims.quote: GSAP uses a default ease of "power1.out".

claims.claim: InstancedMesh is the documented way to draw many identical boxes (voxels) in few draw calls; per-voxel color is written with setColorAt and requires instanceColor.needsUpdate = true afterwards.
claims.quote: Sets the given color to the defined instance. Make sure you set the `needsUpdate` flag of InstancedMesh#instanceColor to `true` after updating all the colors.

claims.claim: For image-to-voxel, the forum-recommended pattern is: scan the image pixels first, keep only non-transparent ones, then allocate the InstancedMesh with exactly that count (so empty pixels cost nothing).
claims.quote: Once known, create instanced mesh with the correct count and set transforms and color.
